issues.title: The API rate limit runs in shadow mode and refuses nothing
issues.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-31 by reading _resolve_mode() rather than trusting the record. The rate limit fix defaults to SHADOW MODE: it measures and logs, it does not refuse. A PRIOR EVIDENCE SWEEP RECORDED THIS AS REMEDIATED, which is the finding worth keeping, because a remediation that only observes reads identical to one that enforces in every artefact except the code. Shadow mode was the owner's deliberate first step so it is not wrong, but it must not be carried as a closed control. Recorded as CLOSED FOR DETECTION and OPEN FOR ENFORCEMENT. The decision needed is when to flip it and what the thresholds are. || OWNER DECISION 2026-09-01: ENFORCE IT. Switch `_resolve_mode()` off shadow so the limit actually refuses, and ship it with the next deploy. Reasoning accepted as put: a limit that refuses nothing is not a control, and the compliance record currently claims a protection that does not exist, which is the worse half of the defect. Sequencing note, not a softening: this lands with the deploy the owner has deferred until the implementations are finished and they have tested, so the code change is made now and takes effect at that deploy. || THE ROW WAS STALE BY THREE WEEKS AND THAT IS THE FINDING, 2026-09-21. directives.text: 'Adopt similar' means STYLE AND DESIGN ONLY; everything else stays as the current build.
Keep the terminal clean; use background agents and parallel execution.
'As per architecture and design' means genuine BEST PRACTICE, not whatever we previously recorded as agreed. A prior decision is evidence, not authority.

No justification-by-assertion in code comments or data files. A file may not state a reason that is not true of the tree.
No conceded field returns without Aparajita signing it off in writing.

RETIRED 2026-09-20 AS WRITTEN, AND RE-STATED. The freeze was lifted by its own condition on 2026-09-10 when the backlog shipped. What survives it is the reporting rule: every status line says DEPLOYED or NOT DEPLOYED, and a fix in the tree is never reported as a fix the owner can see.
directives.note: ORIGINAL TEXT, KEPT SO THE RECORD IS NOT REWRITTEN: "PRODUCTION IS FROZEN until every known defect is fixed. Nothing deploys, however small the change or however green the gates." Owner, 2026-09-08: "nothing must deploy into production untill everything is fixed". Stated while /partners/ was still broken on live and the website was 31 commits behind. || WHY IT IS RETIRED RATHER THAN DELETED. The freeze was conditional on a gap that CLOSED on 2026-09-10, when the backlog shipped. Left standing it reads as a live freeze over a fully shipped tree, which is a directive that blocks work for a reason that no longer exists. || WHAT REPLACES IT, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING. Two things outlive the freeze. FIRST, the reporting rule it was really about: saying "fixed" without saying "and not deployed" is a false report, so every status carries DEPLOYED or NOT DEPLOYED with the board counts beside it. SECOND, the approval rule, which was never part of this directive and is unaffected by retiring it: a push to website main IS a Cloudflare production deploy and needs explicit per-push owner approval with a cost statement. || THE CURRENT GAP IS 46 COMMITS, measured 2026-09-20, main ahead of origin/main. Nothing in this directive authorises closing it.
